terms.name: Attempt
terms.definition: What the risk service is told about a login it is asked to judge: the user id, once the credentials have been checked.

terms.name: Authenticate
terms.definition: Check an email address and a password and answer with a user id or one refusal.

terms.name: Bus
terms.definition: What the relay hands an event to once it is out of the outbox, and what a policy subscribes to. One per domain, in-process today.

terms.name: Conflict
terms.definition: The copy of an aggregate in hand is not what is stored; somebody wrote it since it was read.

terms.name: Credential
terms.definition: An email address and a password, presented together.

terms.name: Email address
terms.definition: The address a user logs in with, normalised and validated on creation.

terms.name: Expiry
terms.definition: The moment a session stops being usable because of time.

terms.name: Locked
terms.definition: The state of a lockout while it refuses. Read off the time; nothing runs when it ends.

terms.name: Lockout
terms.definition: An account refusing passwords for a while after too many wrong ones in a row: five, for fifteen minutes. One per user, from the first wrong password on.

terms.name: Login
terms.definition: Turn a credential into a session: authenticate, ask risk, start.

terms.name: Logout
terms.definition: End the session behind a token, at the user's request. Reason `logout`.

terms.name: Outbox
terms.definition: The table a domain event is written to in the same transaction as the change it describes, and read back out of by the relay - every topic of it, whether or not anything listens.

terms.name: Password hash
terms.definition: What is stored in place of a password: algorithm, cost, salt and digest.

terms.name: Password policy
terms.definition: The rules a new password must satisfy. Applies when a password is created, never when one is checked.

terms.name: Policy
terms.definition: A rule of the form "when this fact happened, do that", spanning two aggregates: revoke sessions on password change. Subscribed to the bus by assembly.

terms.name: Reason
terms.definition: Why a session ended: `logout`, `revoked`, `password-changed`, `risk-blocked`. A closed set.

terms.name: Refusal
terms.definition: The one answer every failed credential check gets: malformed address, unknown address, wrong password, locked account.

terms.name: Register
terms.definition: Create a user from a credential.

terms.name: Revoke
terms.definition: End a session deliberately, with a reason. Terminal; a revoked session never comes back.

terms.name: Risk
terms.definition: The service asked whether a login attempt should go ahead.

terms.name: Session
terms.definition: Proof that a user logged in, how long that proof is good for, and whether it has been taken away.

terms.name: Threshold
terms.definition: The number of wrong passwords in a row that locks an account. One value for everybody.

terms.name: Token
terms.definition: The opaque string a client presents instead of a credential. Carries no claims.

terms.name: User
terms.definition: A person as this context knows them: an id, an email address and a password hash.

terms.name: Validate
terms.definition: Resolve a token to a live session: who is calling and until when. Reads only.

terms.name: Verdict
terms.definition: Risk's answer, in this context's words: `allow` or `block`.

terms.name: Version
terms.definition: The number the store compares before writing an aggregate. Zero means never stored.

terms.name: Address
terms.definition: Where a parcel is going, as the warehouse needs it. A value, copied from the order at dispatch and never refreshed: a parcel already on a van does not move because somebody edited their profile.

terms.name: Awaiting payment
terms.definition: Where every shipment starts. Nothing leaves the warehouse before the ledger says the money moved (ADR core.0002).

terms.name: Capture
terms.definition: Asking the ledger to move the money it was holding for the order, under the order id. Asked by this service when it creates the shipment (ADR core.0003); the ledger's word, used here for the request, while what releases the shipment is the ledger's `PaymentCaptured`.

terms.name: Confirmed order
terms.definition: An order whose payment the ledger authorized, as the order service announces it. The moment a shipment is created; the only thing read off it is the order id.

terms.name: Dispatch
terms.definition: Handing a planned shipment's parcels to the carrier, under a tracking code. The order is asked once more first; a cancelled order's shipment is written off instead.

terms.name: Order
terms.definition: What the shipment is for. Another context owns it, so it is an id here and a question asked over its contract. The table `packages` keeps a foreign key into it, knowingly (ADR core.0001).

terms.name: Package
terms.definition: The row a shipment is kept in. The table's word, not the domain's; the domain says shipment.

terms.name: Parcel
terms.definition: One box. A shipment is one or more of them, and each is scanned on its own, which is why a parcel is an entity: it is followed over time.

terms.name: Released
terms.definition: The money moved; the shipment may be planned onto a route and dispatched. Said by this service, not by the ledger.

terms.name: Route
terms.definition: One van, one day, in the order the stops are driven. The order of the stops is the route: changing it is planning a new one.

terms.name: Scan
terms.definition: One sighting of one parcel: where and when. Append-only; a wrong scan is followed by a right one, and the pair is the history. The first scan after dispatch moves the shipment; the rest do not.

terms.name: Shipment
terms.definition: What is being carried to one address for one order. The aggregate root; its status moves only the way its lifecycle table allows. Created from a confirmed order before anything is packed or addressed.

terms.name: Stop
terms.definition: One place a van stops and what it drops there. Carries a copy of the shipment's address, itself a copy of the order's.

terms.name: Tracking code
terms.definition: What the customer types into a carrier's site. The carrier owns the format; this service only refuses what obviously cannot be one. Also the whole credential for the tracking page.

terms.name: Window
terms.definition: When a van is expected somewhere, as the two ends of a promise to a person.

terms.name: Attempt
terms.definition: Which try at charging one order a payment is. A declined hold is followed by a second, legitimate attempt on the same order, and each is its own payment; the pair of order and attempt is unique (payments.0004).

terms.name: Capture
terms.definition: Moving money the gateway was holding. Writes the pair of postings that accounts for it and says `PaymentCaptured`; the only thing anything waiting to be paid listens for.

terms.name: Decline
terms.definition: The money was not held. Its reason is a closed set: the card was refused, or the order was already cancelled. Not what the gateway said in its own words.

terms.name: Gateway
terms.definition: The card network, as this service asks it: hold, capture, void, refund. A third party behind a port — Stripe, today — and its own words for those four things (a PaymentIntent confirmed, captured, cancelled; a Refund) stay in the adapter. When it does not answer, nothing is decided and nothing is written.

terms.name: Hold
terms.definition: The gateway has reserved the money against an instrument and given back a code that names the reservation. The code is the gateway's handle on the money and never leaves this service: not on an event, not on the wire.

terms.name: Journal
terms.definition: The postings, in the order they were written. Append-only; nothing in it is ever updated, and a correction is another pair.

terms.name: Money
terms.definition: An amount in the minor unit of a currency. The ledger never rounds.

terms.name: Order
terms.definition: What the payment is for. Another context owns it, so it is an id here and nothing more. Asked once, before a hold: a cancelled order is not charged.

terms.name: Payment
terms.definition: What one order owes on one attempt, and everything that has happened to that money. The aggregate root; its status moves only the way its lifecycle table allows.

terms.name: Posting
terms.definition: One side of one movement of money. Comes in balanced pairs.

terms.name: Refund
terms.definition: Money going back against a payment that was captured. Its own aggregate: asked for by somebody else, at another time, for a reason of its own, and there may be several per payment, never adding up to more than was captured.

terms.name: Void
terms.definition: Giving back a hold nobody is going to be charged for. Happens when the order is cancelled; touches nothing that was captured.

terms.name: Basket
terms.definition: The cart's aggregate. An order carries its basket's id and is placed from it exactly once.

terms.name: Bus
terms.definition: NATS JetStream when configured, in process otherwise. One stream per service, named for its subjects.

terms.name: Cancelled
terms.definition: The order will not be fulfilled: the customer asked, or the payment was declined. Terminal.

terms.name: Confirmed
terms.definition: The payment is authorised; the order may be fulfilled.

terms.name: Decline
terms.definition: Ledger's refusal to hold an order's total, with a reason from a closed set. Final for the checkout: it cancels a placed order, never retried.

terms.name: Line
terms.definition: One SKU of the order, how many, and the unit price it was added to the basket at. Copied, never repriced.

terms.name: Money
terms.definition: An amount in the minor unit of a currency.

terms.name: Order
terms.definition: What a basket became at checkout: the lines and the total the customer agreed to, under one lock. The aggregate root.

terms.name: Outbox
terms.definition: The table an event waits in, written in the transaction that produced it, until the relay puts it on the bus.

terms.name: Payments
terms.definition: The ledger that authorises an order's total. A port here; nothing provides it yet.

terms.name: Placed
terms.definition: The order exists and is waiting for its payment to be authorised. Where every order starts.

terms.name: Relay
terms.definition: The loop that moves outbox rows to the bus and marks them published.

terms.name: Adapter
terms.definition: The one file that knows both a port and a peer's generated client, and turns each into the other. Nothing else in the service knows a peer exists.

terms.name: Basket
terms.definition: What the customer is filling, as the cart holds it. The cart calls its lines `items`; the storefront calls them lines, and neither is wrong.

terms.name: Checkout
terms.definition: Freezing a basket at the price it was frozen at. Not an order: the order service places one when it hears the basket was checked out, and a checkout that answered with an order id would be promising something that has not happened.

terms.name: Line
terms.definition: One SKU in a basket or an order, how many of it, and the unit price it was added at.

terms.name: Money
terms.definition: An amount in the smallest unit of a currency, and the currency. Spelled once here, whichever of the three spellings the peers used.

terms.name: Order
terms.definition: What a basket became. Read from the order service and never written here.

terms.name: Order move
terms.definition: One change of an order's state, as it happened. What a subscription yields, and what the bus carried.

terms.name: Order state
terms.definition: Placed, confirmed or cancelled — the three the order service publishes, and no fourth invented for a screen.

terms.name: Peer
terms.definition: Another service in the estate: auth, the cart, the order service, delivery. The storefront talks to four and belongs to none.

terms.name: Port
terms.definition: What a resolver may reach: an interface in `src/ports`, filled at assembly. A resolver holds ports the way a use case elsewhere holds them.

terms.name: Shipment
terms.definition: The parcel on its way, as delivery has it. Its state is delivery's own word, passed on unchanged.

terms.name: Storefront
terms.definition: The context this service belongs to: what a shopper sees, and nothing that decides anything.

terms.name: Viewer
terms.definition: Who the request belongs to. A live session, resolved by auth on every call; nobody, for somebody browsing.

externals.name: Risk
externals.summary: Scores a login attempt before auth issues a session. Nobody in the estate provides it; the copy of its contract beside auth's adapter is narrowed to the one rpc auth runs, and is all the catalog claims about it.

methods.name: Assess
methods.doc: Assess says whether a login attempt should go ahead.

fields.name: user_id
fields.doc:
The user the attempt is for. Auth has already checked the credentials by
the time it asks; risk decides whether that is enough today.

enums.name: Verdict
enums.doc:
Verdict is closed on purpose: a caller switches on it, and a new value is a
contract change rather than a string somebody starts sending.

values.name: VERDICT_BLOCK
values.doc: Refuse the attempt and treat the account as compromised.

externals.name: Stripe
externals.summary: The card network the ledger moves money through. Nobody in the estate provides it; the copy of its document beside the ledger's adapter is narrowed to the four operations the ledger calls, and is all the catalog claims about it.

fields.name: type
fields.doc: The type of error returned. One of `api_error`, `card_error`, `idempotency_error`, or `invalid_request_error`

fields.name: code
fields.doc: For some errors that could be handled programmatically, a short string indicating the [error code](https://docs.stripe.com/error-codes) reported.

fields.name: decline_code
fields.doc: For card errors resulting from a card issuer decline, a short string indicating the [card issuer's reason for the decline](https://docs.stripe.com/declines#issuer-declines) if they provide one.

fields.name: message
fields.doc: A human-readable message providing more details about the error. For card errors, these messages can be shown to your users.

fields.name: param
